node.label: Cheikh Anta Diop
node.date_label: Nations nègres et culture (1954) · Les fondements économiques et culturels d’un futur État fédéral en Afrique noire (1960) · Antériorité des civilisations nègres (1967) · Civilisation ou barbarie (1981)
node.description: A Senegalese historian whose restoration of African historical consciousness connected Egypt, cultural continuity and Pan-African political projects. Tine distinguishes his programme from Senghor’s négritude and reports Dieng’s objections to its treatment of nationhood and cultural borrowing. Diop’s propositions about Egypt and cultural diffusion remain attributed and contested; neither a common African essence nor agreement among African historians is asserted.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Nations nègres et culture (1954); Les fondements économiques et culturels d’un futur État fédéral en Afrique noire (1960); Antériorité des civilisations nègres (1967); Civilisation ou barbarie (1981).
node.scope_note: Read on 2026-10-24: Tine’s introduction, section 2 and conclusion in an author-authorized repository; the publisher’s search-rendered account; BnF/INHA metadata; UCAD’s centenary programme metadata. Diop’s books and Dieng’s original critiques are unread. Claims from 1981 and 1989 are mediated through Tine. No verdict on the population of ancient Egypt is established by publisher praise or a commemorative programme. Tine’s death-year error is excluded; UCAD gives 1986. Original French titles and later translations are not conflated.

people_update.label: Cheikh Anta Diop
people_update.identity_note: Cheikh Anta Diop, Senegalese historian and author identified by Présence Africaine and UCAD’s centenary programme (1923–1986). Distinct from Alioune Diop, the publisher/founder, and from other Diop records; no identity or citation-key merge.

proposed_edges.relationship: Egypt and historical consciousness in Diop’s reconstruction of African history (1954–1981)
proposed_edges.map_label: Egypt and historical consciousness in Diop’s reconstruction of African history (1954–1981)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Tine’s section 2 and the publisher’s account establish Diop’s effort to restore African historical agency by placing ancient Egypt within African history. His diffusionist explanations are his contested theses, not accepted facts about a homogeneous continent.

proposed_edges.relationship: Historical and cultural continuity as a basis for Pan-African independence and federation (1960–1981)
proposed_edges.map_label: Historical and cultural continuity as a basis for Pan-African independence and federation (1960–1981)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Tine distinguishes Diop’s historical-cultural project from Senghor’s négritude while connecting both with anticolonial politics. The 1960 platform is dated by the publisher; no common doctrine or direct influence on other named historians is inferred.

proposed_edges.relationship: Amady Aly Dieng contests Diop’s account of national identity and cultural borrowing (1989–1995), as Tine reports
proposed_edges.map_label: Amady Aly Dieng contests Diop’s account of national identity and cultural borrowing (1989–1995), as Tine reports
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Tine’s section 2 attributes to Dieng objections that Diop privileged race in explaining nationhood and insufficiently distinguished cultural creation from selective borrowing. The originals are unread; this named mediated critique is routed through African historiography, not asserted as its collective verdict.
